name: Action Selection Circuit
short_description: Competes action options based on learned values, urgency signals, and conflict level to select highest-valued action and modulate response timing.

components.name: VALUE_COMPARATOR
components.description: Evaluates and compares learned values of competing action options

components.name: URGENCY_RAMP
components.description: Generates time-dependent urgency signal to accelerate decision with rising pressure

components.name: CONFLICT_DETECTOR
components.description: Detects conflict when multiple actions have similar values

components.name: SELECTION_FINALIZER
components.description: Finalizes action selection based on value, urgency, and conflict; modulates response time

key_references: Cisek, P. (2007). Cortical mechanisms of action selection: The affordance competition hypothesis. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 362(1485), 1585–1599.

Bogacz, R., Brown, E., Moehlis, J., Holmes, P., & Cohen, J. D. (2006). The physics of optimal decision making: A formal analysis of models of performance in two-alternative forced-choice tasks. Psychological Review, 113(4), 700–765.
design_implications: Action choice times increase with conflict; minimize decision burden in time-pressured contexts by reducing option complexity or pre-filtering less-valued alternatives
Urgency-driven decisions trade accuracy for speed; design environments where critical decisions have low time pressure and decision-supporting information is accessible
